contentObjective: I can show I am caught up on Lessons 7.1–7.3 by using each lesson's big idea in mixed practice.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Evidence Boxes
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Park splits 96 pieces of evidence equally among several identical boxes. Each box ends up holding exactly 8 pieces. The equation 8b = 96 represents this situation, where b is the number of boxes. How many boxes did she use? Show your work using inverse operations.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Divide both sides of 8b = 96 by 8: b = 96 ÷ 8 = 12 boxes. Check: 8 × 12 = 96. ✓

vocabulary.definition: Represent a relationship with expressions joined by an equal sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Representar una relación con expresiones unidas por un signo igual.
vocabulary.visual: A $5 fee plus $3 per game for g games: 5 + 3g = total.

vocabulary.definition: A math sentence with an equal sign showing both sides are the same.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una oración matemática con un signo igual que muestra que ambos lados son iguales.
vocabulary.cloze: A math sentence that says two amounts are equal, with an = sign, is an ___.

examples.why: It has an equal sign showing two equal amounts.
That is an expression because it has no equal sign.

vocabulary.term: Solve One-Step Addition and Subtraction Equations
vocabulary.termEs: Resolver ecuaciones de suma y resta de un paso
vocabulary.definition: Use one inverse addition or subtraction operation to isolate the variable.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Usar una operación inversa de suma o resta para aislar la variable.

vocabulary.termEs: Resolver ecuaciones de multiplicación y división
vocabulary.definition: Use inverse multiplication or division to isolate the variable.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Usar la multiplicación o división inversa para aislar la variable.

vocabulary.definition: Two math actions that undo each other, like × and ÷.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos operaciones que se deshacen entre sí, como × y ÷.
vocabulary.visual: Multiplication and division are inverses: 3 × 7 = 21, so 21 ÷ 3 = 7
vocabulary.cloze: An operation that undoes another, like division undoing multiplication, is an ___.

examples.text: Dividing by 4 to undo multiplying by 4
Multiplying by 4 to undo multiplying by 4
examples.why: Multiplying again does not undo it.

vocabulary.definition: A letter that stands for a number that is unknown or can change.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una letra que representa un número desconocido o que puede cambiar.
vocabulary.visual: In n + 3 = 10, the letter n stands for the unknown number (n = 7)
vocabulary.cloze: A letter that stands for an unknown number is a ___.

vocabulary.definition: To add equal groups again and again.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Sumar grupos iguales una y otra vez.
vocabulary.cloze: To undo dividing by a number, I ___ both sides by that number.

launch.narrative: Missed a lesson — or just want a refresher? This catch-up station reviews Lessons 7.1–7.3: 7.1 Write Equations, 7.2 Solve One-Step Addition and Subtraction Equations, 7.3 Solve Multiplication and Division Equations. Read the Big Ideas, warm up with the review problem, then prove you're caught up in the mixed practice.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 7.1–7.3
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 7.1: Find the unknown, choose a variable, then turn the words into symbols around an equal sign. • 7.2: Undo the operation with its inverse, and do it to both sides to keep the equation balanced. • 7.3: Divide to undo multiplying, and multiply to undo dividing — always on both sides.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 7.1 — Write Equations: Find the unknown, choose a variable, then turn the words into symbols around an equal sign.
Lesson 7.2 — Solve One-Step Addition and Subtraction Equations: Undo the operation with its inverse, and do it to both sides to keep the equation balanced.
Lesson 7.3 — Solve Multiplication and Division Equations: Divide to undo multiplying, and multiply to undo dividing — always on both sides.

weDo.title: Quick guided checks — one from each lesson
lines: From 7.1: New clue: 'A number plus 5 equals 9.' What is the unknown?
From 7.2: Solve x − 4 = 9. Is x being added or subtracted?
From 7.3: Solve x ÷ 4 = 9. Is x multiplied or divided?

youDo.title: Show you're caught up
lines: The practice below mixes problems from Lessons 7.1–7.3. Each problem is tagged with its lesson number.
Stuck on one lesson's problems? Open that lesson from the curriculum menu for the full re-teach.

explore.instructions: Solve each equation by showing your work. Use inverse operations to isolate the variable.
hints: For multiplication equations like 3x = 21, the inverse is division. Divide both sides by the coefficient.
For division equations like x / 4 = 9, the inverse is multiplication. Multiply both sides by the divisor.
explore.label: Complete the table to solve each equation. Show your inverse operation and work.

discourse.prompt: How do you decide whether to multiply or divide to solve an equation?
discourse.sentenceFrame: When I see ___ in the equation, I know to ___ both sides because the inverse of ___ is ___.

diagram.intro: Now write the solving steps on paper-style lines — I'll check each one keeps the same solution.

optional.stem: (Lesson 7.1) A witness statement reads: 'A number c of security cameras plus 6 more equals 19.' Which equation matches?
optional.explanation: 'Plus 6 more' means + 6 and 'equals 19' means = 19, so c + 6 = 19. Check: 13 + 6 = 19.
choiceFeedback: Check the operation: "plus" means add, not multiply.
That shows removing 6. The words say plus 6.
The problem asks you to add, not divide.
optional.stemEs: Una declaración de un testigo dice: 'Un número c de cámaras de seguridad más 6 más es igual a 19.' ¿Cuál ecuación corresponde?
optional.explanationEs: 'Más 6 más' significa + 6 y 'es igual a 19' significa = 19, así que c + 6 = 19. Comprueba: 13 + 6 = 19.
hints: An equation matches the words piece by piece: a starting amount, an operation, and what the total equals.
Name the unknown first — c is the number of cameras you do not know yet — then translate 'plus 6 more' into an operation.
Begin writing it: c comes first, then the operation for 'plus 6 more', then the equals sign with 19. Pick the operation the words describe.
hintsEs: Una ecuación corresponde a las palabras parte por parte: una cantidad inicial, una operación y a cuánto es igual el total.
Nombra primero la incógnita: c es el número de cámaras que aún no conoces. Luego traduce 'más 6 más' a una operación.
Empieza a escribirla: primero va c, luego la operación de 'más 6 más', y después el signo igual con 19. Elige la operación que describen las palabras.

optional.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides: x = 15 − 7 = 8. Check: 8 + 7 = 15 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 7 from both sides: x = 15 − 7 = ___.
That is the number being added in the equation, not the unknown value. Subtract it from both sides to uncover x.
The two numbers got multiplied. Addition is undone by subtraction, so take 7 away from both sides instead.
optional.explanationEs: Resta 7 en ambos lados: x = 15 − 7 = 8. Comprueba: 8 + 7 = 15 ✓
hints: The equation shows something being added to x, and the equal sign means both sides have the same value.
Use the inverse operation: whatever is added to x should be subtracted from both sides.
Subtract 7 from both sides. The left side becomes just x, and the right side becomes 15 − 7 — finish that subtraction.
hintsEs: La ecuación muestra que algo se le suma a x, y el signo igual significa que ambos lados tienen el mismo valor.
Usa la operación inversa: lo que se le suma a x debe restarse en ambos lados.
Resta 7 en ambos lados. El lado izquierdo queda solo como x y el derecho queda como 15 − 7 — termina esa resta.

optional.stem: (Lesson 7.3) Vault A is sealed with 4x = 32. Crack the lock: what is x?
optional.explanation: The 4 is multiplying x, so divide both sides by 4: x = 32 / 4 = 8. Check: 4 x 8 = 32.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. The 4 is multiplying x, so divide both sides by 4: x = 32 ÷ 4 = ___.
That is 32 − 4. The 4 is multiplied by x, so division is what undoes it.
That is 32 + 4. Adding will not isolate x when x is being multiplied.
optional.stemEs: La bóveda A está sellada con 4x = 32. Abre la cerradura: ¿cuánto vale x?
optional.explanationEs: El 4 está multiplicando a x, así que divide ambos lados entre 4: x = 32 / 4 = 8. Comprobación: 4 x 8 = 32.
hints: An equation stays balanced when the same operation is done to both sides.
The 4 is multiplied by x, so undo it with the inverse operation.
Divide both sides by 4, which gives x = 32 ÷ 4. Finish that division, then check by multiplying back.
hintsEs: Una ecuación se mantiene equilibrada cuando se hace la misma operación en los dos lados.
El 4 está multiplicando a x, así que deshazlo con la operación inversa.
Divide los dos lados entre 4, lo que da x = 32 ÷ 4. Termina esa división y comprueba multiplicando al revés.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.1) Which equation represents: 'A number plus 12 equals 30'?
approaching.explanation: 'Plus' means addition, so the equation is n + 12 = 30.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. 'Plus' means addition, so the equation is n + 12 = ___.
Check the operation: "plus" means add, not multiply.
The problem asks you to add, not divide.
hints: Find the operation word in the sentence. What does 'plus' tell you to do with the number and 12?
Let n stand for the unknown number, then translate each phrase into symbols: 'a number' becomes n, 'plus 12' names an operation, 'equals 30' becomes = 30.
Build it left to right: n, then the symbol for 'plus', then 12, then '= 30'. Which choice matches that exact order?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Un número más 12 es igual a 30'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Más' significa suma, así que la ecuación es n + 12 = 30.
hintsEs: Halla la palabra de operación en la oración. ¿Qué te dice 'más' que hagas con el número y el 12?
Deja que n represente el número desconocido y luego traduce cada frase a símbolos: 'un número' se vuelve n, 'más 12' nombra una operación y 'es igual a 30' se vuelve = 30.
Ármalo de izquierda a derecha: n, luego el símbolo de 'más', luego 12, luego '= 30'. ¿Qué opción coincide con ese orden exacto?

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.1) Which equation represents: 'Seven less than a number is 18'?
approaching.explanation: 'Seven less than a number' means start with the number and subtract 7: n − 7 = 18.
choiceFeedback: Start with the variable, then subtract — not the other way.
The clue says "fewer" or "less" — use subtraction, not addition.
Use subtraction for "fewer" or "less," not division.
hints: 'Seven less than a number' is tricky — the number comes FIRST, and then 7 is taken away from it.
'Less than' flips the wording: '7 less than n' means start at n and subtract 7, not start at 7 and subtract n.
Write the number first: n, then subtract 7, then set it equal to 18. Which choice is built in that order?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál ecuación representa: 'Siete menos que un número es 18'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Siete menos que un número' significa empezar con el número y restar 7: n − 7 = 18.
hintsEs: 'Siete menos que un número' es tramposo: el número va PRIMERO y luego se le quitan 7.
'Menos que' invierte el enunciado: '7 menos que n' significa empezar en n y restar 7, no empezar en 7 y restar n.
Escribe el número primero: n, luego resta 7 y luego iguálalo a 18. ¿Qué opción está armada en ese orden?

approaching.explanation: Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 15 − 9 = 6. Check: 6 + 9 = 15 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 15 − 9 = ___.
That number is already showing in the equation as the amount being added, not the unknown. Undo the addition by subtracting it from both sides.
That is the total after 9 was added, not the starting value. Work backward from the total by subtracting 9 from both sides.
hints: x has 9 added to it. To get x alone, you need to UNDO that addition.
Use the inverse operation: subtraction undoes addition. Whatever you do, do it to BOTH sides to keep the balance.
Subtract 9 from both sides: x = 15 − 9. Then check by adding 9 back to your result — do you land on 15?
approaching.explanationEs: Resta 9 en ambos lados: x = 15 − 9 = 6. Comprueba: 6 + 9 = 15 ✓
hintsEs: A x se le suman 9. Para dejar x sola, tienes que DESHACER esa suma.
Usa la operación inversa: la resta deshace la suma. Lo que hagas, hazlo en AMBOS lados para mantener el equilibrio.
Resta 9 de ambos lados: x = 15 − 9. Luego comprueba sumando 9 de nuevo a tu resultado: ¿llegas a 15?

approaching.explanation: Add 7 to both sides: y = 20 + 7 = 27. Check: 27 − 7 = 20 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Add 7 to both sides: y = 20 + 7 = ___.
That is the amount being subtracted, not the value of y. Undo the subtraction by adding it to both sides.
The two numbers got multiplied. Subtraction is undone by addition, so add 7 to both sides instead.
hints: Look at what's happening to y: 7 is being SUBTRACTED. Which operation undoes subtraction?
Add the same amount to both sides so the equation stays balanced and y ends up alone.
Add 7 to both sides: y = 20 + 7. Check your result: does it minus 7 give back 20?
approaching.explanationEs: Suma 7 en ambos lados: y = 20 + 7 = 27. Comprueba: 27 − 7 = 20 ✓
hintsEs: Mira lo que le pasa a y: se le RESTA 7. ¿Qué operación deshace una resta?
Suma la misma cantidad a ambos lados para que la ecuación siga equilibrada y y quede sola.
Suma 7 a ambos lados: y = 20 + 7. Comprueba tu resultado: ¿restarle 7 devuelve 20?

approaching.explanation: Divide both sides by 6: x = 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Check: 6 × 7 = 42 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Divide both sides by 6: x = 42 ÷ 6 = ___.
That is 42 − 6, a subtraction. The 6 is multiplying x, so the operation that undoes it is division.
That is 42 × 6. Multiplying again moves you further from x instead of isolating it.
hints: 6x means 6 TIMES x — the variable is being multiplied by 6.
Division undoes multiplication. Divide both sides by 6 to leave x alone.
Compute 42 ÷ 6, then check by multiplying your answer by 6 — do you get 42 back?
approaching.explanationEs: Divide ambos lados entre 6: x = 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Comprobación: 6 × 7 = 42 ✓
hintsEs: 6x significa 6 POR x: la variable está multiplicada por 6.
La división deshace la multiplicación. Divide ambos lados entre 6 para dejar x sola.
Calcula 42 ÷ 6 y luego comprueba multiplicando tu respuesta por 6: ¿obtienes 42 de vuelta?

approaching.explanation: Multiply both sides by 3: n = 8 × 3 = 24. Check: 24 / 3 = 8 ✓
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Multiply both sides by 3: n = 8 × 3 = ___.
That is 8 − 3. Since n is being divided by 3, the operation that undoes it is multiplication.
That is the number n is divided by, not n itself. Undo the division to isolate n.
hints: n is being DIVIDED by 3. Which operation undoes division?
Multiply both sides by 3 — the ÷3 and ×3 cancel each other, leaving just n.
Compute 8 × 3, then check: your answer divided by 3 should give 8.
approaching.explanationEs: Multiplica ambos lados por 3: n = 8 × 3 = 24. Comprobación: 24 / 3 = 8 ✓
hintsEs: n está siendo DIVIDIDA entre 3. ¿Qué operación deshace una división?
Multiplica ambos lados por 3: el ÷3 y el ×3 se cancelan y queda solo n.
Calcula 8 × 3 y luego comprueba: tu respuesta dividida entre 3 debe dar 8.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 7.1) A detective found some fingerprints on Monday and 14 more on Tuesday, for a total of 30. Which equation represents this?
onLevel.explanation: The detective's Monday fingerprints (f) plus 14 more equals 30: f + 14 = 30.
choiceFeedback: The 14 were found in addition to Monday's, so they are added, not subtracted.
Multiplying would mean the Monday prints were repeated 14 times over. The words say 14 more prints were found, which is about combining amounts.
Dividing splits the prints into 14 equal groups, which is not what happened on Tuesday. Reread what the detective did with the 14 new prints.
hints: Monday's fingerprints are the unknown f. On Tuesday she found 14 MORE, and the two days together total 30.
'More' means the two amounts combine into one total. Combining to reach a total is addition, not multiplying or dividing.
Write it in story order: f (Monday) plus 14 (Tuesday) equals 30 (total). Which choice shows that sum?
onLevel.stemEs: Un detective encontró algunas huellas dactilares el lunes y 14 más el martes, para un total de 30. ¿Cuál ecuación representa esto?
onLevel.explanationEs: Las huellas del lunes (f) más 14 más es igual a 30: f + 14 = 30.
hintsEs: Las huellas del lunes son la incógnita f. El martes encontró 14 MÁS, y los dos días juntos suman 30.
'Más' significa que las dos cantidades se combinan en un total. Combinar para llegar a un total es suma, no multiplicación ni división.
Escríbelo en el orden de la historia: f (lunes) más 14 (martes) es igual a 30 (total). ¿Qué opción muestra esa suma?

onLevel.title: (Lesson 7.1) Crack the Equation Error

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: A number of case files divided by 3 equals 6.

workedExample.label: Choose a variable
workedExample.work: Let n be the number of case files.

onLevel.correctWork: 'Divided by 3' means division, not multiplication. The correct equation is n / 3 = 6, not 3n = 6. Check: 18 / 3 = 6.
hints: Does 'divided by 3' tell you to multiply by 3 or split into 3 equal groups?
'A number divided by 3' is n / 3, so the equation is n / 3 = 6.
onLevel.titleEs: Descifra el error de la ecuación
onLevel.explanation: The clue says the case files are divided by 3, but the equation 3n = 6 multiplies instead. Dividing means splitting n into 3 equal groups, so the equation is n / 3 = 6, and 18 / 3 = 6 confirms it.
onLevel.explanationEs: La pista dice que los expedientes se dividen entre 3, pero la ecuación 3n = 6 multiplica en su lugar. Dividir significa repartir n en 3 grupos iguales, así que la ecuación es n / 3 = 6, y 18 / 3 = 6 lo confirma.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 7.2) A shirt costs $d. After a $15 discount, it costs $38. What is d?
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you subtracted 15 from 38. Instead: d − 15 = 38 → d = 38 + 15 = $53.
That is the price after the discount, not the original price. The original price has to be larger, so add the discount back on.
The discount was not added back fully. Set up d − 15 = 38, then add 15 to both sides and combine carefully.
hints: The $15 discount was taken OFF the original price d, and $38 is what's left after the discount.
Write the story first: d − 15 = 38. Then undo the subtraction — the original price should be MORE than $38, not less.
Add the $15 discount back onto the $38 sale price: d = 38 + 15. Which choice matches that total?
onLevel.stemEs: Una camisa cuesta $d. Después de un descuento de $15, cuesta $38. ¿Cuánto vale d?
hintsEs: El descuento de $15 se le QUITÓ al precio original d, y $38 es lo que queda después del descuento.
Escribe primero la historia: d − 15 = 38. Luego deshaz la resta: el precio original debe ser MÁS de $38, no menos.
Vuelve a sumar los $15 del descuento al precio de oferta de $38: d = 38 + 15. ¿Qué opción coincide con ese total?

onLevel.title: (Lesson 7.2) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Choose inverse
workedExample.work: The inverse of − 13 is + 13, so add 13 to both sides.

onLevel.correctWork: The inverse operation was correct, but the addition was done wrong: 28 + 13 = 41, not 31. So y = 41. Check: 41 − 13 = 28 ✓
hints: The plan (add 13 to both sides) is right. Recheck the arithmetic in the last step.
Add carefully: 28 + 13 = 41, so y = 41, not 31.
onLevel.explanation: The plan was correct — adding 13 to both sides is the right inverse for y − 13 = 28 — but the "Simplify" step adds wrong. 28 + 13 = 41, not 31, so y = 41. Substituting back confirms it: 41 − 13 = 28, while 31 − 13 would give 18.
onLevel.explanationEs: El plan era correcto —sumar 13 en ambos lados es la inversa adecuada para y − 13 = 28—, pero el paso "Simplify" suma mal. 28 + 13 = 41, no 31, así que y = 41. Sustituir de regreso lo confirma: 41 − 13 = 28, mientras que 31 − 13 daría 18.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 7.3) A detective splits 54 clues equally among 9 case files. The equation 9c = 54 represents this. What is c?
onLevel.explanation: Divide both sides by 9: c = 54 ÷ 9 = 6 clues per file.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Divide both sides by 9: c = 54 ÷ 9 = ___ clues per file.
That is 54 − 9. Sharing equally is a division, so undo the multiplication by dividing.
That is the number of case files, not the number of clues in each one. Divide the total by the number of files.
hints: c is the number of clues in EACH file, and 9 files with c clues each make all 54 clues.
9c = 54 multiplies c by 9 — undo it by dividing both sides by 9, not by adding or subtracting.
Compute 54 ÷ 9 (what times 9 makes 54?). Your answer should be much smaller than 54 — clues per file, not the total.
onLevel.stemEs: Un detective reparte 54 pistas en partes iguales entre 9 expedientes. La ecuación 9c = 54 representa esta situación. ¿Cuánto vale c?
onLevel.explanationEs: Divide ambos lados entre 9: c = 54 ÷ 9 = 6 pistas por expediente.
hintsEs: c es el número de pistas en CADA archivo, y 9 archivos con c pistas cada uno forman las 54 pistas.
9c = 54 multiplica c por 9: deshazlo dividiendo ambos lados entre 9, no sumando ni restando.
Calcula 54 ÷ 9 (¿qué por 9 da 54?). Tu respuesta debe ser mucho menor que 54: son pistas por archivo, no el total.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 7.3) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Choose operation
workedExample.work: n is in a fraction, so I will divide both sides by 4.

onLevel.correctWork: n is divided by 4, so the inverse is MULTIPLICATION. Multiply both sides by 4: n = 12 × 4 = 48. Check: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 ✓
hints: The student divided again instead of multiplying. Division does not undo division.
To undo ÷ 4, you must × 4. Multiply both sides by 4 to isolate n.
onLevel.explanation: Dividing again does not undo division. Since n is divided by 4, multiply both sides by 4: n = 12 × 4 = 48, and 48 ÷ 4 = 12 confirms it. The answer 3 is a clue on its own — n has to be bigger than 12, not smaller, because it was cut into fourths.
onLevel.explanationEs: Volver a dividir no deshace una división. Como n está dividida entre 4, multiplica ambos lados por 4: n = 12 × 4 = 48, y 48 ÷ 4 = 12 lo confirma. La respuesta 3 es una pista por sí sola: n tiene que ser mayor que 12, no menor, porque fue partida en cuartos.

extending.title: (Lesson 7.1) Find the Equation Error
extending.correctWork: 'Twice' means multiply by 2, not add 2. The correct equation is 2n = 16.
hints: What does 'twice' really mean — adding or multiplying?
'Twice a number' means 2 times the number, so the equation is 2n = 16.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la ecuación
extending.explanation: The operation was named wrong at the start: 'twice' was called addition, which led to n + 2 = 16. Twice a number means two of that number, which is multiplication, so the equation is 2n = 16.
extending.explanationEs: La operación se nombró mal desde el inicio: se dijo que 'twice' era una suma, lo que llevó a n + 2 = 16. El doble de un número significa dos veces ese número, que es multiplicación, así que la ecuación es 2n = 16.

extending.title: (Lesson 7.2) Find the Equation Error
extending.correctWork: Inverse of subtraction is ADDITION. Add 18 to both sides: x = 45 + 18 = 63.
hints: Step 2 says the inverse of subtraction is subtraction. Is that right?
To undo −18, you need +18, not another −18. Addition undoes subtraction.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error de la ecuación
extending.explanation: The "Identify inverse" step claims subtraction undoes subtraction, which pushes the equation further from the answer instead of isolating x. Addition undoes subtraction, so add 18 to both sides of x − 18 = 45: x = 45 + 18 = 63. Checking, 63 − 18 = 45, while the answer 27 would give 9.
extending.explanationEs: El paso "Identify inverse" afirma que la resta deshace la resta, lo que aleja la ecuación de la respuesta en lugar de despejar x. La suma deshace la resta, así que suma 18 en ambos lados de x − 18 = 45: x = 45 + 18 = 63. Al comprobar, 63 − 18 = 45, mientras que la respuesta 27 daría 9.

extending.title: (Lesson 7.3) Find the Equation Error
extending.correctWork: Inverse of division is MULTIPLICATION. Multiply both sides by 5: x = 12 × 5 = 60. Check: 60 / 5 = 12 ✓
hints: Step 2 says the inverse of division is division. Is that correct?
To undo ÷ 5, you need × 5. Multiplication undoes division.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error en la ecuación
extending.explanation: The inverse named in that step is wrong: division is undone by multiplication, not by more division. Multiply both sides by 5 to get x = 12 × 5 = 60, and 60 / 5 = 12 checks. Dividing again shrank x to 2.4, far below the 12 it was supposed to produce.
extending.explanationEs: La operación inversa que se nombró en ese paso está mal: la división se deshace con multiplicación, no con más división. Multiplica ambos lados por 5 para obtener x = 12 × 5 = 60, y 60 / 5 = 12 comprueba. Volver a dividir redujo x a 2.4, muy por debajo del 12 que debía producir.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Solve Multiplication and Division Equations is applying the SAME operation again instead of the inverse — for example, seeing 6x = 42 and multiplying both sides by 6 to get x = 252, instead of dividing by 6 to get x = 7. Before you submit, ask: did I use the OPPOSITE operation shown in the equation, and did I apply it to both sides?

diagram.title: Splitting the $63 Kit Bill
diagram.caption: The top bar is the whole bill ($63); below it we split it into equal $7 groups — counting the 9 groups shows k = 63 ÷ 7 = 9 kits.

connect.scenario: A detective ordered fingerprint kits for her team. Each kit costs $7, and the total bill was $63. The equation 7k = 63 represents this situation, where k is the number of kits.
connect.promptQuestion: How many kits did the detective order? How did inverse operations help you solve this?
connect.prompt: The detective ordered ___ kits because 7k = 63 means k = 63 ÷ ___ = ___.

check.explanation: Divide both sides by 7: k = 63 ÷ 7 = 9 kits.
Multiplication and division are inverse operations. Since k was multiplied by 7, divide both sides by 7.

connect.modelAnswer: 7k = 63. Division undoes multiplication, so divide both sides by 7: k = 63 ÷ 7 = 9 kits. Check: 7 × 9 = 63. ✓

exitTicket.explanation: Subtract 2.8 from both sides: p = 9.1 − 2.8 = 6.3. Check: 6.3 + 2.8 = 9.1 ✓ (11.9 comes from adding instead of subtracting; 7.7 comes from subtracting each decimal place without regrouping — 9 − 2 = 7 and, without borrowing, 8 − 1 = 7; 3.25 comes from dividing 9.1 ÷ 2.8 instead of subtracting.)
choiceFeedback: You added 2.8 — undo it by subtracting from both sides.
Recheck your subtraction: 9.1 − 2.8 in the tenths place.
Subtract 2.8 from 9.1 — that's not the result.
hints: p has 2.8 added to it. To get p alone you must undo the addition — decimals follow the same rule as whole numbers.
Subtract 2.8 from both sides. Line up the decimal points and watch the tenths place for regrouping.
Set up 9.1 − 2.8: you can't take 8 tenths from 1 tenth, so borrow from the 9 first. Then check by adding 2.8 back to your result.

steps.promptEs: Usa x para el valor desconocido: ___.

hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: Use x for the unknown: x.
parallelPractice.explanation: Use x for the unknown: x. “plus 2” becomes + 2. Write the equation: x + 2 = 4.
parallelPractice.stemEs: Escribe una ecuación: un número x más 2 es igual a 4.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Usa el modelo visual y completa un paso a la vez.
Empieza así: Usa x para el valor desconocido: x.
